scenes.visual: Title card: WATER CHOOSES.

scenes.tts: Geometry allows a few shapes. So what chooses among them?
scenes.visual: Loose helices and strands drift on screen. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: Geometry allows a few shapes. So what chooses among them?

scenes.tts: Mostly, water does. Picture one oily side chain, like leucine's, sitting in water.
scenes.visual: A grey oily blob labelled leucine sits in a field of small water molecules (V-shaped symbols).
scenes.narration: Mostly, water does. Picture one oily side chain, like leucine's, sitting in water.

scenes.tts: Water molecules hydrogen bond to each other all the time, in a shifting network.
scenes.visual: Dashed lines flicker between water symbols, forming and breaking.
scenes.narration: Water molecules hydrogen bond to each other all the time, in a shifting network.

scenes.tts: Next to the oily surface, they cannot hydrogen bond to it.
scenes.visual: Water symbols touching the blob show no dashed line to it.
scenes.narration: Next to the oily surface, they cannot hydrogen bond to it.

scenes.tts: So the water in contact forms a tighter, more ordered network around it, like a cage.
scenes.visual: The water around the blob stiffens into a neat ring. Label: ordered water.
scenes.narration: So the water in contact forms a tighter, more ordered network around it, like a cage.

scenes.tts: Ordered water has lost freedom. That is lost entropy.
scenes.visual: Label beside the ring: lost freedom = lost entropy.
scenes.narration: Ordered water has lost freedom. That is lost entropy.

scenes.tts: Now bring two oily side chains together. Less oily surface faces the water.
scenes.visual: A second blob slides next to the first; the two cages merge into one smaller ring.
scenes.narration: Now bring two oily side chains together. Less oily surface faces the water.

scenes.tts: Less water has to be caged. The freed water tumbles away and gains entropy.
scenes.visual: Several water symbols break free of the ring and tumble off. Label: entropy gained.
scenes.narration: Less water has to be caged. The freed water tumbles away and gains entropy.

scenes.tts: That gain drives the oily groups together. It is called the hydrophobic effect.
scenes.visual: Title: hydrophobic effect.
scenes.narration: That gain drives the oily groups together. It is called the hydrophobic effect.

scenes.tts: A common mistake is that oil is pulled to oil. But oily groups attract water about as well.
scenes.visual: A struck-through label: oil pulls oil. Beside it, two small equal arrows: oil to oil, oil to water.
scenes.narration: A common mistake is that oil is pulled to oil. But oily groups attract water about as well.

scenes.tts: Oily groups are pushed together by water, not pulled together by each other.
scenes.visual: Arrows from the surrounding water push the blobs together. Label: pushed by water.
scenes.narration: Oily groups are pushed together by water, not pulled together by each other.

scenes.tts: So in a water-soluble protein, the nonpolar side chains end up buried in a core.
scenes.visual: A schematic chain collapses; grey beads gather in the middle.
scenes.narration: So in a water-soluble protein, the nonpolar side chains end up buried in a core.

scenes.tts: Polar and charged side chains sit on the surface, in the water.
scenes.visual: Colored charged beads stay on the outside, touching the water.
scenes.narration: Polar and charged side chains sit on the surface, in the water.

scenes.tts: This packs the whole chain into a compact shape. That is tertiary structure.
scenes.visual: The compact blob, cut open to show the grey core. Label: tertiary structure.
scenes.narration: This packs the whole chain into a compact shape. That is tertiary structure.

scenes.tts: Burial also helps explain helices and sheets. Buried backbone groups lose their water partners.
scenes.visual: A stretch of backbone sinks into the core; its C=O and N–H groups lose their water.
scenes.narration: Burial also helps explain helices and sheets. Buried backbone groups lose their water partners.

scenes.tts: A buried polar group with no partner costs free energy.
scenes.visual: One unpaired buried group glows orange. Label: costly.
scenes.narration: A buried polar group with no partner costs free energy.

scenes.tts: The cheapest fix is for the backbone to bond to itself. Helices and sheets are the regular ways to do that.
scenes.visual: The buried stretch coils into a helix; its groups pair up with dashed lines and turn green.
scenes.narration: The cheapest fix is for the backbone to bond to itself. Helices and sheets are the regular ways to do that.

scenes.tts: Burial does not stop at one chain. Folded chains can bury oily surface against each other.
scenes.visual: Two folded blobs approach; their grey surface patches meet.
scenes.narration: Burial does not stop at one chain. Folded chains can bury oily surface against each other.

scenes.tts: That assembly is quaternary structure. Hemoglobin is two alpha and two beta subunits, working as one.
scenes.visual: Four blobs assemble, labelled α, α, β, β. Label: quaternary structure, hemoglobin.
scenes.narration: That assembly is quaternary structure. Hemoglobin is two alpha and two beta subunits, working as one.

scenes.tts: Now return to sickle cell. Valine puts an oily residue on the surface, where a charged one was.
scenes.visual: On one β subunit, a red charged bead becomes a grey bead labelled Val6.
scenes.narration: Now return to sickle cell. Valine puts an oily residue on the surface, where a charged one was.

scenes.tts: That makes a new sticky patch. Once oxygen is released, the patch fits an oily pocket on a neighbouring hemoglobin.
scenes.visual: O2 dots leave and each hemoglobin shifts shape, opening a grey pocket. The grey patch docks into the pocket of the next hemoglobin, which docks onto the next, forming a rod.
scenes.narration: That makes a new sticky patch. Once oxygen is released, the patch fits an oily pocket on a neighbouring hemoglobin.

scenes.tts: Sickle cell is an unwanted contact between whole hemoglobins, built by the same rule.
scenes.visual: The rod lengthens into a fiber. Label: an unwanted interface.
scenes.narration: Sickle cell is an unwanted contact between whole hemoglobins, built by the same rule.

scenes.tts: One more surprise. A folded protein is only marginally more stable than the unfolded coil.
scenes.visual: Two energy levels, folded and unfolded, drawn close together. Label: small gap.
scenes.narration: One more surprise. A folded protein is only marginally more stable than the unfolded coil.

scenes.tts: The chain gives up a lot of freedom to fold. Its contacts and freed water only just pay for it.
scenes.visual: A balance scale: freedom given up versus contacts made and water freed, almost level.
scenes.narration: The chain gives up a lot of freedom to fold. Its contacts and freed water only just pay for it.

scenes.tts: So heat can undo a fold. The melting temperature is where half the molecules are unfolded.
scenes.visual: A steep S-shaped melt curve: fraction folded against temperature. A marker at the midpoint labelled Tm.
scenes.narration: So heat can undo a fold. The melting temperature is where half the molecules are unfolded.

scenes.tts: Here is the test. A buried leucine becomes aspartate. Or a surface lysine becomes arginine. Which one melts lower?
scenes.visual: Two panels: core Leu → Asp; surface Lys → Arg. On-screen question: which melts lower?
scenes.narration: Here is the test. A buried leucine becomes aspartate. Or a surface lysine becomes arginine. Which one melts lower?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: The buried aspartate. It is charged, with no water to bond with, and it breaks up the oily packing.
scenes.visual: The core panel: the Asp glows orange in the grey core. Its melt curve slides to a lower Tm.
scenes.narration: The buried aspartate. It is charged, with no water to bond with, and it breaks up the oily packing.

scenes.tts: The surface swap trades one positive charge for another, still in water. Stability barely changes.
scenes.visual: The surface panel: the melt curve stays where it was.
scenes.narration: The surface swap trades one positive charge for another, still in water. Stability barely changes.

scenes.tts: Water pushes oil inward. That burial builds the core and the interfaces.
scenes.visual: End card. LINE: Water pushes oily side chains inward, and that burial builds the core, the interfaces and a fold that is only just stable.
scenes.narration: Water pushes oil inward. That burial builds the core and the interfaces.
